strengths: Addresses a timely and practically important problem: KV cache quantization tailored specifically to long-CoT reasoning LLMs, which differs meaningfully from the short-context regime that prior KV quantization work has focused on.

Clear and well-motivated problem decomposition into two specific failure modes (cumulative quantization error from long decoding sequences, and short-context calibration mismatch due to RoPE's low-frequency channels), each addressed with a targeted technique.

Extensive empirical evaluation spanning model scales from 7B to 70B (DeepSeek-R1-Distill family and QwQ-32B) and multiple challenging reasoning benchmarks (AIME-2024/2025, CMIMC-2024, LiveCodeBench), showing consistent and often large improvements over strong baselines (KIVI, RotateKV, MiKV) at aggressive 2-bit/4-bit settings.

Thoughtful ablations that isolate design choices, e.g., comparing three bit-width shrinking strategies (Direct/Modified/Equivalent Right Shift) and varying calibration length/position scaling factor for the positional interpolation technique.

Reasonable and practical engineering solutions: an efficient closed-form 'Equivalent Right Shift' bit-shrinking operation and an Integer Programming formulation for block-wise bit allocation that can be solved quickly with off-the-shelf solvers.

Appendix sensitivity analysis across many model architectures (LLaMA- vs Qwen-based) adds some interpretability and shows consistent qualitative trends (deeper blocks more sensitive, Qwen first block particularly sensitive).
weaknesses: Novelty is largely incremental/combinatorial: progressive precision reduction, Taylor-based mixed-precision sensitivity allocation, and positional interpolation are each adaptations of existing ideas (e.g., LLM-MQ style sensitivity-based allocation, RoPE positional interpolation from Chen et al. 2023) rather than fundamentally new techniques.

All results are from 'fake quantization' simulation; there is no real hardware memory footprint or latency/throughput evaluation, so the practical system-level benefit (including overhead of the progressive shrinking/shifting operations and the IP solve) is unverified.

The main comparison setup is somewhat confounded: PM-KVQ's progressive scheme uses higher average precision earlier in generation and converges to the target Fbit near full context length, while baselines use fixed low bit-width throughout; this asymmetric memory-usage pattern, while explained, muddies a strictly iso-memory comparison and its exact accounting is not fully quantified (e.g., average bits used over the full trajectory).

Ablation results for positional interpolation are modest and show fragility: benefit at s=4 is small (~1.66% pass@1) and larger scaling factors (s=16) actually hurt performance, raising questions about robustness and how the scaling factor should be chosen in practice without extensive tuning.

The block-wise memory allocation and bit-width shrinking ablations are validated on only one model/one benchmark (DeepSeek-LLaMA-8B on AIME-2024), limiting confidence that these findings generalize across the diverse model family tested elsewhere in the paper.

The method assumes the maximum context length is known a priori to compute the progressive quantization schedule/memory budget; it's unclear how this generalizes to real serving scenarios with variable-length requests and dynamic batching.

The paper explicitly does not address Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA), which is used in the actual full DeepSeek-R1/V3 models (only distilled GQA-based models are tested), limiting the generality of the claims for the most relevant frontier reasoning models.

No comparison to other mixed-precision or dynamic-bit-width KV cache methods beyond MiKV; the baseline set, while reasonable, is not exhaustive of recent related work in adaptive/progressive quantization.

strengths: Addresses a timely and practical problem: KV cache memory overhead for long-CoT reasoning LLMs, which is increasingly important as reasoning models generate very long outputs.

Three well-motivated technical components (progressive quantization, block-wise memory allocation via Integer Programming, calibration with positional interpolation) directly target the two identified failure modes (cumulative error and short-context calibration mismatch).

Rigorous mathematical proof (Appendix D) establishing the equivalence of the proposed 'Equivalent Right Shift' bit-shrinking operation to dequantize-then-requantize, which supports the correctness of the core algorithmic trick.

Extensive experiments across a wide range of model scales (7B to 70B) and multiple reasoning/coding benchmarks (AIME-2024/2025, CMIMC, LiveCodeBench), plus additional non-reasoning (IFEval) and sparse-attention (QuestAttention) evaluations in the appendix.
Reasonably thorough ablations isolating the contribution of each component (bit-shrinking strategy, block sensitivity, positional interpolation length/scaling factor).

Comparisons against multiple relevant baselines (KIVI, RotateKV, MiKV, KVTuner) under matched hardware/batch-size constraints, and efficiency (throughput) measurements demonstrating practical speedups over 16-bit inference.
Code release and detailed experimental configuration aid reproducibility.
weaknesses: Limited fundamental novelty: progressive/mixed-precision quantization and positional-interpolation-based calibration are combinations/adaptations of existing techniques (PI from Chen et al. 2023, mixed-precision allocation similar to prior LLM/diffusion quantization work) rather than fundamentally new ideas.

PM-KVQ's throughput is consistently *worse* than KIVI (2.45–16.18% lower per the paper's own numbers); the headline throughput gains (2.73–5.18x) are relative to unquantized 16-bit models, not to the strongest quantization baseline, which somewhat overstates the efficiency contribution.

The practical mechanics of progressive quantization in a batched-serving setting (sequences of different lengths reaching different bit-width transition points simultaneously) are not clearly explained or evaluated at scale, raising reproducibility/implementation-complexity concerns.

Method explicitly does not support Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), which is used by the actual DeepSeek-R1 model (only tested on distilled GQA-based variants), limiting applicability to the most relevant production model.

Block-wise memory allocation is evaluated with only two candidate bit-widths per model (e.g., {2,4} or {4,8}), which is a fairly coarse mixed-precision granularity and may understate/overstate the real benefit of the IP-based allocation approach.

The improvement from positional interpolation alone is modest (~1.66% pass@1 in the reported ablation), and no fair comparison is given against simply calibrating with equally long non-interpolated sequences under matched compute budget for larger models.

Statistical rigor is limited: AIME datasets have only 30 problems per year, and while means and std are reported, no significance testing is done to confirm that reported gains (some quite small, e.g., <1%) are meaningful versus noise.

The specific batch-size choices used to showcase progressive quantization/block-wise allocation benefits appear selected to create underutilized-memory scenarios; it is unclear how consistently these benefits materialize across a broader range of real-world deployment configurations beyond the two hand-picked batch sizes per model shown in Section C.5.

strengths: Clearly identifies a practically important problem: KV cache quantization under-explored for long-CoT reasoning models where generation can extend to 32K+ tokens.
Extensive empirical evaluation spanning 7B to 70B models and multiple reasoning/coding benchmarks (AIME, CMIMC, LiveCodeBench, IFEval), with several baselines (KIVI, RotateKV, MiKV, KVTuner).
The 'Equivalent Right Shift' bit-width shrinking operation is accompanied by a rigorous mathematical equivalence proof, which is a nice piece of careful engineering.
Reasonable set of ablations (bit-shrinking strategy, block sensitivity, PI scaling factor, hardware configurations, sparse-attention compatibility) that help interpret the individual components.
Reports throughput numbers, not just accuracy, giving a more complete efficiency picture.
weaknesses: The three core components (progressive/staged bit-width reduction, Taylor-sensitivity-based mixed-precision allocation via integer programming, positional-interpolation calibration) are each individually incremental extensions of well-known prior ideas (staged quantization, sensitivity-based mixed precision as in Li et al./Zhao et al./KVTuner, and position interpolation from Chen et al. 2023); the paper offers limited unifying algorithmic novelty beyond combining these known ingredients.

The paper's own analysis (Appendix C.8) shows that progressive quantization mainly benefits shorter responses that never reach the memory budget; for the target long-CoT scenario (>16K tokens), the higher-precision benefit is confined to only the first 16K tokens, undermining the claimed relevance to genuinely long generations.

PM-KVQ effectively uses more memory on average during generation than fixed-bitwidth baselines (staying at higher precision until the budget is exhausted), which is a natural memory-accuracy tradeoff rather than a fundamentally more efficient quantization scheme; the accuracy gains over baselines at matched peak memory are therefore somewhat expected rather than surprising.

Reported throughput of PM-KVQ is consistently worse than KIVI (2.45-16.18% degradation), and the headline '2.73-5.18x over 16-bit' figure is driven mainly by batch-size increase from quantization in general rather than being a distinctive contribution of the proposed method.

Baseline comparisons at 2-bit are somewhat uninformative since RotateKV and MiKV completely fail (0% accuracy) in several settings, which raises questions about whether these baselines were properly tuned/implemented at that extreme setting, making the 'up to 8%' improvement claims potentially cherry-picked from cases where competitors collapse entirely.

The method is only validated on GQA-based distilled models (Qwen/LLaMA backbones), not on the actual DeepSeek-R1 model which uses Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA); this is explicitly noted as a limitation and significantly reduces the practical relevance of the results to the flagship long-CoT models the paper is motivated by.

The comparison protocol allows PM-KVQ two batch-size configurations per model (to showcase both progressive quantization and block-wise allocation) while baselines are often shown under a single or truncated configuration (e.g., Table 7 truncates KIVI output when it exceeds memory), which complicates fair, apples-to-apples comparison and may bias reported gains upward.

The quantization bit-width granularity is restricted to powers of two (16/8/4/2), limiting the flexibility and generality of the block-wise memory allocation approach in real deployment scenarios with arbitrary memory budgets.
